clusters.name: Walter's move across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move to Sorrel Valley in March 1952, within a year: June grew homesick and wrote to her sister Edna daily; Walter spent long hours away from her in the orchard; Glen got into fights at his new school; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land; June kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter and June had rows over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, her anxiety dropping and her functioning rising; the period settles there.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968, within months: Walter drank heavily most nights; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan and clashed; Glen took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969; Ida's heart trouble was found and she stopped working at the bakery. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, his functioning rising; the period settles there.

clusters.name: Glen's cannery closure, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975, within months: Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard; he and Marian had loud fights at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora kept to her room and spoke little to her mother; Walter drank again after six years off it. By June 1976, Nora ate again and made the track team, her functioning rising; the period settles there.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into the household, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990, within months: Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals; Sam worked late and kept out of the rows; Sam took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Sam had rows most nights. By June 1991, Wilma took a flat in town; Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, her symptom dropping; the period settles there.
